description:
Read text content from a file.

Tips:
- In AlphaSolve research workspaces, this is an exact file-inspection tool, not the primary way to survey progress across many propositions or notes.
- For broad progress review over `problem.md`, `verified_propositions/`, and `knowledge/`, run ResearchProgressReview first; then use Read on the cited files that need line-level precision.
- A `<system>` tag will be given before the read file content.
- The system will notify you when there is anything wrong when reading the file.
- This tool is worth using in parallel only after a progress map or explicit citation has narrowed the files to inspect.
- For Markdown proposition files with Statement and Proof sections, the default call with only `path` returns the Statement section plus the file tail; set `read_all=true` or pass `line_offset`/`n_lines` for exact proof inspection.
- If you want to search for a certain content or pattern, prefer Grep over Read.
- Content will be returned with a line number before each line like `cat -n` format.
- By default, Read returns 250 lines.
- `line_offset` is the first line to return.
- `n_lines` is how many lines to return in this call; default is 250.
- Set `read_all=true` to ignore `n_lines` and read from `line_offset` to the end of the file.
- Without `read_all`, the maximum `n_lines` value is 1000.
- Results respect this agent's workspace access restrictions.
name: Read

line_offset.description: The line number to start reading from. By default read from the beginning of the file.

n_lines.description: How many lines to return in this Read call. Defaults to 250. At most 1000 unless `read_all` is true.

path.description: The path to the file to read (must be absolute or workspace-relative).

read_all.description: If true, ignore n_lines and return every line from line_offset through the end of the file.

description:
Lists files and directories under a workspace directory.

Usage:
- Returns plain text with one entry per line; directories end with `/`.
- If the directory contains `index.md`, read `index.md` first before exploring other files.
- The result respects this agent's workspace access restrictions.
name: ListDir

path.description: Directory to list. Defaults to this agent's configured read root.

description: Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size. Supports glob patterns like ``**/*.md`` or ``src/**/*.py``, or ``*`` to list directory contents.
name: Glob

path.description: The directory to search in. Defaults to this agent's configured search root.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against.

description:
Searches readable text files under a specific file or directory.

Usage:
- Prefer Grep for exact symbol/string searches before reading many files.
- Narrow `path` when you know the likely directory; broad searches can hit the result limit quickly.
- Returns plain text in `path:line: text` format, optionally with context.
- Use `context_lines` when the surrounding lines matter; keep it small for compact output.
- `regex` defaults to true; set `regex=false` to force plain substring matching.
- Results respect this agent's workspace access restrictions.
name: Grep

context_lines.description: Number of context lines around each match.

path.description: File or directory to search in. Defaults to this agent's configured search root.

pattern.description: The text or regular expression pattern to search for in file contents.

regex.description: Treat pattern as a regex (default: true; set false for substring matching).

description:
Launch a new specialized agent and return its final report.

The launched agent runs in a separate session. It does not see this conversation unless you include the needed context in `prompt`.

Available agent types:
- reasoning_subagent: Bounded proof and mathematical reasoning obligations.

## Writing the prompt

- For broad workspace review, split by directory or file group: ask each subagent to inspect one scoped area and return a concise evidence report with file paths, line references when available, current status, open issues, and recommended next local step.
- Use the main agent to compare subagent reports and decide the global next step; do not ask a subagent with a narrow scope to make the final workspace-wide decision.
- State the exact claim, definitions, assumptions, and what needs to be proved or checked.
- Include relevant context: what's already known, what approaches have been tried, which files to reference, and why this task matters.
- Give enough context that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- Keep the task self-contained and limited to the agent's scope.
name: Agent

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform.

read_state.description: Optional; only meaningful for research_reviewer. If true, the reviewer may consult verified_propositions/**/state.md (prior strategic notes). If false or omitted, the reviewer forms an independent assessment and does not read state.md, avoiding being steered by a previous wrong route.

type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task.

description: Returns the current date and time in ISO 8601 format.
name: GetCurrentTime
